problem: The five-whys Claude Code plugin (v0.2.0) is rated 8/10 instead of 10/10.
context:
The plugin (v0.2.0, published 2026-09-13) generates a complete 5x5x5x5x5 Five Whys tree (3,905 reasons) with one root agent and 25 branch agents dispatched in waves of at most 20, validates every fragment with a stdlib Python script, and assembles one JSON tree plus index.md and hygiene.json. Analysis is left to the user by requirement.

v0.2.0 was built by running v0.1.0 on its own 6/10 rating and classifying all 3,905 reasons against a 31-item improvement catalog. It added: configurable shape and a smoke preset, capped waves, attempt tracking, per-run and per-tier model choice, cost estimates with confirmation, non-blocking lexical hygiene flags, sibling-aware branch prompts, rewritten agent instructions (specificity, stated assumptions, evidence reading), prompt files, status/show/partial assembly, a check log, 35 unit tests with CI, an eval case, a release checklist and a self-improvement ledger.

Evidence behind the 8/10 rating:
1. No full 5x5 run has happened on v0.2.0; only a 39-reason smoke run. Published cost/time numbers come from v0.1.0.
2. The new SKILL.md orchestration (flag parsing, thin-context question, confirmation, wave loop) has never been executed by a model from /five-whys; the script and agents were driven by hand.
3. The eval case has never been run.
4. Hygiene is lexical word overlap; in the smoke run it missed a real cross-branch paraphrase. Deep cross-branch convergence is still undetected.
5. Token estimates are scaled from one run; model-tier quality trade-offs are unmeasured.
6. Surface area grew: about 700 script lines and 14 options.
7. Ledger classification was agent judgment; 1,298 of 3,905 reasons were dispositioned as outside the plugin's control or past history.
